name: hippocratics-brain-seat-of-mind
friendly_name: Hippocratics Put Mind in the Brain
description: Greek physicians of the Hippocratic school declared the brain, not the heart, the seat of thought, joy and madness.

name: bethlem-hospital-first-patients
description: A London priory began housing the mentally ill and became the infamous asylum that gave English the word bedlam.

name: weyer-witches-mentally-ill
description: A Dutch physician argued in print that many accused witches were mentally ill and needed medicine, not punishment.

name: mesmer-animal-magnetism
description: A Viennese doctor treated patients with supposed magnetic fluids, launching the craze that later led to hypnosis.

name: gall-founds-phrenology
description: A German physician claimed mental faculties live in distinct brain regions and can be read from bumps on the skull.

name: phineas-gage-accident
description: An iron rod blasted through a railway foreman's skull and he survived, though his personality was said to change.

name: broca-speech-area
description: A French surgeon linked damage in one region of a patient's left frontal brain to the loss of speech.

name: wundt-leipzig-psychology-lab
description: A German professor founded a Leipzig laboratory devoted to measuring the mind, making psychology an experimental science.

name: cajal-neuron-doctrine
friendly_name: Cajal Shows the Neuron Is Separate
description: A Spanish anatomist drew nerve cells as individual units rather than a continuous web, founding the neuron doctrine.

name: james-principles-of-psychology
description: A Harvard thinker's two-volume work introduced the stream of consciousness and shaped the new science of mind.

name: binet-simon-intelligence-test
description: A French psychologist and his colleague built the first practical test to identify schoolchildren needing extra help.

name: watson-behaviorist-manifesto
description: An American psychologist declared that psychology should study only observable behaviour, not introspection.

name: little-albert-experiment
description: Researchers taught a baby to fear a white rat by pairing it with a loud noise, a notorious study of learned emotion.

name: rorschach-inkblot-test
description: A Swiss psychiatrist published ten symmetrical inkblots that people interpret, meant to reveal hidden personality traits.

name: moniz-first-lobotomy
description: A Portuguese neurologist had surgeons cut into a patient's frontal lobes to treat mental illness, a method later condemned.

name: first-electroconvulsive-therapy
description: Italian doctors gave a patient with schizophrenia a brief electric shock to the head to induce a therapeutic seizure.

name: maslow-hierarchy-of-needs
description: An American psychologist arranged human motivations in a pyramid, from food and safety up to self-fulfilment.

name: cade-lithium-for-mania
description: An Australian psychiatrist found that a simple salt calms manic patients, beginning modern mood-stabiliser therapy.

name: chlorpromazine-first-antipsychotic
description: French doctors found a drug that calmed psychosis, emptying wards of restraints and opening the age of psychiatric medicine.

name: patient-hm-memory-loss
description: Surgery to cure a man's epilepsy removed parts of both temporal lobes and left him unable to form new memories.

name: milgram-obedience-experiment
description: Volunteers told to give what seemed painful shocks to a stranger mostly kept obeying the experimenter.

name: kubler-ross-five-stages-grief
description: A Swiss-American psychiatrist published a bestseller describing five stages people pass through when facing death.

name: stanford-prison-experiment
description: Students playing guards and prisoners in a basement mock jail turned cruel so fast that the study was stopped early.

name: rosenhan-pseudopatients
description: Healthy volunteers feigned hearing voices to enter psychiatric hospitals, then acted normally yet stayed for weeks.

name: gardner-multiple-intelligences
description: A Harvard psychologist argued that intelligence has several independent forms, such as musical, spatial and interpersonal.

name: prozac-reaches-market
description: An American drug company launched an antidepressant that became one of the most prescribed and discussed medicines ever.

name: optogenetics-switches-neurons
description: Researchers showed that light-sensitive proteins let them switch chosen brain cells on and off with flashes of light.
